answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through a bounded random walk, limiting influence from distant or weakly endorsed identities. A sybil grove may amplify internal endorsements, but an external cut of conductance φ creates a bottleneck: mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the walk mass crossing it, thereby bounding aggregate voting weight by φ, walk length, and boundary size. Honest attestations ripple through the graph, while each endorsement thread cannot bypass the cut.
